text:
Alexis Lafrenière has become the kind of player the Rangers hoped for when they took him first overall in 2020: 10 goals and 22 points in 24 games, more than 18 minutes a night, and a two-way game Evolving-Hockey rated 29th among all forwards last season, often against the other team's best. ESPN is already writing about what his breakout means for the years ahead.

The last few weeks are the other side of it. He has one goal in his last ten games, with his chances dipping below his usual rate, and Bolavip reports Mike Sullivan has had to defend him through it. Some of the earlier pace was finishing: he's shooting 19.6%, above our talent range of roughly 12 to 17%, and his points rate is above the top of the range too.

So both stories are true. The player is better than the one who arrived, and the slump is partly the bill for a hot start. Watch the shot volume, two or three a night in most of these games; goals tend to follow shots, at a saner pace than the start.
headline: Lafrenière's breakout is real, and so is the dip
